name: v7-pairs
note: V7 step 3, one variable. Evidence (experiments/v7, development tasks only): round 54's failures are mostly a trained function written instead of the requested one (38 of 68 clean dev + unseen-v1 failures); the function it writes is the trained one whose description shares the most words with the prompt (wording percentile 0.90, name 0.80, code 0.81; training frequency 0.49, no relation). On the neighbour diagnostic set it passes 1/19 tasks worded like a trained function with one detail changed, and prefers the neighbour's code by 16 nats on average; adding input-output examples or a behavioural constraint does not help (0/19, 0/19), and naming a neighbouring function in the prompt makes it write that function (17/38 answers compute the neighbour, from 9). The mapping from the deciding words of a task to the deciding tokens of its code is what fails. Arms P1 and P0 train on the same examples (half: curriculum programs that have a sibling, i.e. another constant, condition or direction in the same family, built by ycode.lm.idioms.pair_examples; half: the C-sized legacy mix) and differ only in the loss weight of the answer tokens where the program's code differs from its sibling's: 20 in P1 (about 20% of the pair examples' loss weight, 1.6 tokens per example), the usual body weight 3 in P0. Same seed, steps, learning rate, layers and evaluation; curriculum families, architecture and duration unchanged between arms. No pair program shares an AST skeleton with a held-out item (dev, unseen-v1, unseen-v2, benchmark) or with the neighbour diagnostic set. Disk: 3.7 GB free and no old checkpoint may be removed, so each run writes only its final weights, as the base-referenced bf16 file that evaluation loads and that is kept (train.final_bf16, tested to load the same weights as the usual fp32 checkpoint cast to bf16); a run interrupted before its last step restarts.
decision: The V6 rule, unchanged: a candidate replaces round 54 only if every seed beats its all_clean (29/168), the mean gain is >= 3 items and no failure category loses >= 3 clean items round 54 passes (items_lost). Screening (development tasks only; the runner's metric is unseen_clean = clean dev /44 + unseen-v1 /53, because unseen-v2 is evaluated only for a candidate that passes screening): P1 goes on to a second seed and the full evaluation only if it beats P0 and round 54 on the neighbour set's original prompts and does not lose dev + unseen-v1 items against P0. The benchmark is reported only.
